item.title: eMudhra To Exit Certificate Business As Security Flaw Triggers Distrust
item.dc:creator: Shraddha Goled
item.description: Bengaluru-based cybersecurity company eMudhra, which recently found itself at the centre of a security key issue, has announced plans to…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based cybersecurity company eMudhra, which recently found itself at the centre of a security key issue, has announced plans to voluntarily wind down its global secure sockets layer and transport layer security (SSL/TLS) certificate business.

In a filing, the company said that the decision followed a security incident in which a researcher discovered that the private keys of eight intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates were weak enough to be recovered. The discovery prompted browser root programmes, including Google and Mozilla, to distrust eMudhra’s certificates, affecting its global TLS business.

eMudhra said it revoked the affected CAs within 14 hours of discovering the incident and disclosed it promptly. It added that no end-entity certificates had been issued by the affected CAs, its infrastructure remained uncompromised and no data was breached.

“The impact has been quite severe over the last 24-48 hours. Given the risk to the rest of the business and our obligations as a publicly listed company, the board felt it was prudent to withdraw from this business,” Kaushik Srinivasan, cofounder, told Inc42.

The company also cited rising compliance costs, declining returns and limited revenue contribution as the reason behind the move. The segment accounts for around 1% of its global revenue. The company reported revenues of ₹701.6 Cr in FY26.

The segment’s future commercial prospects also triggered the closure. With Let’s Encrypt offering free TLS certificates and Cloudflare planning to do the same, Srinivasan said the commercial return from the business looks limited, particularly as browser guidelines move towards 90-day certificates.

“The board evaluated the social media reaction, but also took cognisance of the ROI, future potential and competitive landscape,” he said, adding that eMudhra would focus on more complex customer problems in areas such as AI and quantum computing.

What Does This Mean For eMudhra’s Customers

eMudhra said existing customers would be transitioned to alternative certificate providers free of charge over the next three to four weeks, with the company working with other certificate partners to avoid service disruptions. 

Srinivasan said the distrust of its G3 ECC root had already affected around 30,000 certificates in the US, which were transitioned to its G1 RSA root. To be sure, G1 and G3 are eMudhra’s root certificate hierarchies: G1 uses RSA cryptography, while G3 uses elliptic curve cryptography (ECC). Google and Mozilla distrusted G3 as a precaution following the security incident, while G1 continues to operate and issue certificates. All certificates in India and various adjoining markets were issued from the G1 root.

However, the G3 root distrust impacted an undisclosed US client. “It resulted in around 30,000 certificates in the US market being affected because they were under ECC. We had to transition them to RSA. Following our announcement, we have to transition them to another provider. We are actively working on that,” Srinivasan said.

The Incident That Shook The World

On October 17, researcher Wayne notified browser root programmes and eMudhra that he had recovered the private keys corresponding to eight intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates. The keys had been generated with insufficient randomness, making them vulnerable to reconstruction. 

Such keys could potentially be used to issue fraudulent certificates for websites or software, although eMudhra said none of the eight intermediates had issued end-entity certificates. Six were intended for TLS and two for software signing. Browser root programmes from companies like Mozilla and Google moved to block the affected TLS intermediates.

eMudhra, at the time, said the certificates were created on April 30, 2025, and had undergone independent audits, though it did not name the auditors or disclose the audit scope. The company said only one affected intermediate was deployed in production, none had issued end-entity certificates, and all eight had been revoked.

The incident prompted a worldwide reaction, casting aspersions on eMudhra’s security controls and the reliability of its certificate issuance processes. Security experts were also unsatisfied with eMudhra’s clarification on the matter. 

Responding to this, Srinivasan said that it was a script error and a human oversight problem; no hardware problem was found. “We will share the facts in due course, and this will also be verified through independent research.  It was a one-off, a bad day. That’s exactly what happened.”

Notably, the flaw went undetected for around 18 months, spanning two independent audit cycles. 

Srinivasan said eMudhra will now appoint an auditor to prepare the final report on the incident, which would take 2-3 weeks. Further, the company would strengthen internal accountability, maker-checker controls and independent reviews for critical processes such as key generation. The company is also exploring AI-based checks to detect weaknesses and flag potential errors.

item.title: Swiggy To Begin Instamart Inventory Model Transition, Eyes Pivot Within Three Quarters
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Over two months after attaining the IOCC (Indian-Owned and Controlled Company) tag, Swiggy announced that it will shortly commence transitioning…
item.content:encoded:
Over two months after attaining the IOCC (Indian-Owned and Controlled Company) tag, Swiggy announced that it will shortly commence transitioning its quick commerce business, Instamart, to an inventory-led model. 

In its Q2 shareholders letter, the company announced that it will pivot Instamart to the inventory model by mid-Q3 FY27. The transition is expected to take 2-3 quarters to complete. Swiggy expects the transition to improve Instamart’s working capital cycle by 8-10 days. 

“As we have mentioned in our previous communications, this has the potential to add 80 bps to Instamart’s contribution margin when fully rolled-out while giving us greater flexibility and control over assortment, pricing, availability and day-to-day operations,” the company said.

The inventory model will give Instamart greater control over product assortment, pricing, availability and day-to-day operations in comparison to its current model where Instamart operates as a marketplace hosting seller entities. 

Eternal’s quick commerce arm Blinkit was the first to complete the inventory-led model pivot. The company has seen a significant improvement in its bottom line performance since then. Blinkit has emerged as the largest revenue contributor for Eternal, contributing ₹19,152 Cr to the company’s total ₹24,138 Cr operating revenue for Q2 FY27.

Swiggy has been bidding to undertake a similar transition for some time now. Its initial May 2026 special resolution to become an IOCC failed after receiving 72.36% of shareholder votes in favor, narrowly missing the required 75% threshold

It managed to get shareholder approval to enable the transition earlier in August. Today, the company said its domestic ownership has increased to over 58%.

Instamart Margins Under Pressure

Swiggy’s quick commerce margins further weakened in the September quarter (Q2 FY27). 

The quick commerce business reported a contribution margin of -1% of gross order value (GOV), compared with -0.2% in Q1 FY27 on the back of  higher spending on pricing and customer retention.

Instamart’s adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹895 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹778 Cr in the preceding quarter. Its net order value rose 34.8% year-on-year to ₹6,594 Cr, while Swiggy added 69 net dark stores during the quarter, taking the network to 1,240 stores across 133 cities.

“Contribution margin was -1.0% of GOV within the range guided earlier, as we added 69 net stores, taking the network to 1,240 stores across 133 cities, and invested in differentiated assortment, availability and service quality,” the management added.

While Instamart NOV grew 13.4% sequentially to  reach ₹6,594 Cr and orders were up 29.3% YoY to 130 Mn, the adjusted EBITDA loss rose to ₹895 Cr in the quarter. 

At the consolidated level, Swiggy’s revenue from operations increased 36.1% YoY to ₹7,571 Cr in Q2 FY27. Its net loss narrowed 15.6% year-on-year to ₹922 Cr, but widened from ₹791 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Shares of Swiggy ended today’s trading session 5.01% lower at ₹211.30 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: [Update] Jio Platforms IPO Ends Day 2 With 5.57X Subscription, QIBs Lead Demand
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Update | October 22, 19:35 IST Jio Platforms’ ₹30,213 Cr IPO ended the second day of bidding with 5.57X subscription,…
item.content:encoded:
Update | October 22, 19:35 IST

Jio Platforms’ ₹30,213 Cr IPO ended the second day of bidding with 5.57X subscription, receiving bids for 110.03 Cr shares against 19.75 Cr shares on offer, according to BSE data.

Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led demand, bidding for 65.15 Cr shares against 4.90 Cr shares reserved for the category, taking subscription to 13.29X. The non-institutional investor (NII) portion was subscribed 5.97X, with bids for 21.76 Cr shares.

Within the NII category, the portion reserved for applications exceeding ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 6.76X, while the segment for applications above ₹2 Lakh and up to ₹10 Lakh was booked 4.38X. 

The retail portion was subscribed 1.54X, receiving bids for 13.11 Cr shares against 8.50 Cr shares reserved for the category.

Meanwhile, the employee and shareholder portions were subscribed 2.10X and 4.05X, respectively.

Original | October 22, 12:28 IST

Reliance Industries’ digital services arm Jio Platforms’ IPO was subscribed 3.65X on the second day of bidding, with institutional investors leading demand and the retail portion crossing full subscription.

Investors bid for 72.05 Cr shares against 19.75 Cr shares on offer as of 12:03 IST, according to BSE data.

The qualified institutional buyers’ (QIBs) portion was subscribed 9.42X, receiving bids for 46.16 Cr shares against an allocation of 4.91 Cr shares. Domestic financial institutions, including banks and insurance companies, accounted for 25.92 Cr shares, followed by foreign institutional investors at 16.18 Cr shares and mutual funds at 3.19 Cr shares.

The non-institutional investors’ (NIIs) portion was subscribed 2.85X, getting bids for 10.38 Cr shares against 3.64 Cr shares reserved for the category. Within this, the portion for bids exceeding ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 3.06X, while that for bids above ₹2 Lakh and up to ₹10 Lakh was booked 2.43X.

Retail investors bid for 9.39 Cr shares against an allocation of 8.50 Cr shares, translating to 1.10X subscription. The employee and shareholder portions were subscribed 1.71X and 2.38X, respectively.

On its first day of bidding yesterday, the public issue was subscribed 3.15X, driven by strong demand from institutional investors.

India’s Largest Public Offering

Jio Platforms has set a price band of ₹1,065-₹1,119 per share for the IPO, which closes tomorrow. The ₹30,213 Cr (about $3.2 Bn) offering is set to surpass Hyundai Motor India’s ₹27,870 Cr issue as India’s largest IPO.

At the upper end of the price band, Jio Platforms would be valued at around ₹10.3 Lakh Cr (about $108 Bn).

Ahead of the public offering, the company raised ₹8,109.8 Cr from anchor investors, allotting 7.25 Cr shares at ₹1,119 apiece. Domestic mutual funds acquired around 2.48 Cr shares through 95 schemes, while insurance companies and pension funds picked up 97 Lakh shares.

The anchor book also included Fidelity, Allianz, BlackRock, the Government of Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, and Goldman Sachs.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to 27 Cr equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component. Jio plans to use ₹27,500 Cr of the proceeds to prepay certain borrowings of its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd (RJIL), and deploy the remaining funds for general corporate purposes.

The proposed repayment covers three external commercial borrowing facilities worth a combined ₹29,971 Cr, raised from a consortium of Indian and international lenders, including SBI, Bank of America and First Abu Dhabi Bank. The loans funded 5G infrastructure deployment and spectrum acquisition, with repayments scheduled between March and June 2028 and interest rates ranging from 1.40% to 5.13% per annum. 

The IPO comes as Jio expands beyond telecom connectivity into fixed broadband, cloud services, enterprise solutions, and AI. RJIL had 533.3 Mn customers as of June 30, 2026, while its fixed broadband subscriber base stood at 28.6 Mn.

Jio Platforms reported a 9.2% increase in consolidated net profit to ₹7,764 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹7,110 Cr a year earlier. Operating revenue rose 11.8% YoY and 2.4% QoQ to ₹39,173 Cr.

For FY26, operating revenue rose nearly 15% YoY to ₹1.47 Lakh Cr, while net profit increased 15.1% YoY to ₹30,049 Cr.

item.title: BlueStone Slips Into ₹4.4 Cr Loss In Q2, Revenue Jumps 45% YoY
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Omnichannel jewellery retailer BlueStone slipped into the red in the second quarter of FY27, reporting a consolidated net loss of…
item.content:encoded:
Omnichannel jewellery retailer BlueStone slipped into the red in the second quarter of FY27, reporting a consolidated net loss of ₹4.4 Cr against a net profit of ₹6 Cr in the preceding quarter. However, its loss narrowed nearly 92% from ₹52.1 Cr in the year-ago quarter.

Operating revenue rose 45% to ₹745 Cr from ₹513.6 Cr in Q2 FY26. On a sequential basis, revenue edged up 1.1% from ₹736.8 Cr.

Including other income of ₹24.4 Cr, BlueStone’s total income stood at ₹769.4 Cr during the September quarter.

Total expenses increased 34% YoY and 3.7% QoQ to ₹772.4 Cr. 

BlueStone said its adjusted profit after tax for the quarter stood at ₹19.6 Cr as against an adjusted net loss of ₹26.8 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Its adjusted PAT increased by 42% QoQ. 

The company said Q2 FY27 was its fourth consecutive quarter of profitability, adding, “Adjusted PAT shows how our operating performance is reaching the bottom line as the business scales … This demonstrates that the business scale and operating leverage we have spoken about in earlier commentary are now flowing through the bottom line.” 

It reported ₹53.5 Cr in pre-IndAS EBITDA, a 234% YoY jump. However, its pre-IndAS EBITDA narrowed by around 2.3% on a sequential basis.

“Over the past year, a key focus area has been our entry-level price points, where gold price inflation had dislocated our offering. Our redesigned range is now taking more shelf space in our stores, and this quarter we saw early signs of that effort paying off: new customers contributed a larger share of revenue than in the previous quarter, and AOV moderated accordingly,” the company observed in its commentary. 

Separately, the company’s board approved raising up to ₹300 Cr through non-convertible debentures (NCDs) on a private placement basis, in one or more tranches. The proceeds will be used to refinance a portion of its existing debt and meet capital expenditure, working capital, and general corporate requirements. 

Store Network Expands Further

BlueStone ended September with 379 stores across 146 cities, adding 27 stores over the past three months.

All seven cities it entered during Q2 were in Tier II and III markets. It also called out its investment in its new 3,200 sq ft flagship store in Kolkata. 

The company noted that it had front-loaded its expansion ahead of the festival season, adding, “While the opportunity remains large, we continue to expand in a calibrated way, both by entering new cities and by adding density in existing ones. We remain on track with our stated distribution objectives for the year.”

Its customer base crossed 1 Mn during the quarter, reaching 10.24 Lakh at September-end, up 19.3% YoY. Repeat customers contributed 56.3% of quarterly revenue, compared with 51.4% a year earlier.

On a standalone basis, BlueStone’s same-store sales grew 28% YoY during Q2, while operating revenue increased 43.9% to ₹738.1 Cr. 

Shares of BlueStone ended the day 2.78% higher at ₹760.45.

item.title: Zetwerk IPO: Kae Capital, Kalysta Bag 38.3X Returns, Lightspeed Pockets ₹440 Cr
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Early backers Kae Capital Fund II and Kalysta Capital Fund II bagged 38.3X returns on shares sold through manufacturing company…
item.content:encoded:
Early backers Kae Capital Fund II and Kalysta Capital Fund II bagged 38.3X returns on shares sold through manufacturing company Zetwerk’s IPO, emerging among the biggest gainers in its offer for sale (OFS).

At ₹151 apiece, the upper end of the IPO price band, the sale price was 38.3 times the two funds’ weighted average acquisition cost of ₹3.94 per share.

Kae Capital Fund II pocketed ₹196.3 Cr by selling around 1.3 Cr shares, while Kalysta Capital Fund II received ₹63.3 Cr from the sale of 41.9 Lakh shares.

Both investors retain sizeable holdings after the sale. Kae Capital Fund II holds 4.3 Cr shares valued at ₹649.3 Cr at ₹151 apiece, while Kalysta Capital Fund II holds 1.4 Cr shares worth ₹211.4 Cr.

The payouts come after Zetwerk’s IPO closed with 3.06X subscription, attracting bids for 56.62 Cr shares against 18.50 Cr shares on offer. The company’s shares are scheduled to list on the exchanges tomorrow. 

Meanwhile, Peak XV and Lightspeed sold shares through multiple investment vehicles, with returns varying across their funds.

Peak XV pocketed a combined ₹359.3 Cr through two vehicles – Peak XV Partners Investments V and Peak XV Partners Growth Investments III. Peak XV Partners Investments V sold around 1.8 Cr shares for ₹271.8 Cr, clocking a 23.9X return multiple. It retains 12.2 Cr shares valued at ₹1,842.2 Cr at the IPO price.

Peak XV Partners Growth Investments III received ₹87.5 Cr from the sale of around 58 Lakh shares, realising a 3.3X return multiple. It retains 4 Cr shares worth ₹604 Cr. Together, the two funds held a 12.1% stake in Zetwerk before the OFS.

Lightspeed, which invested through three vehicles, collectively pocketed around ₹440 Cr.

Lightspeed Venture Partners Select IV Mauritius sold around 1.4 Cr shares for ₹211.4 Cr, while Lightspeed India Partners II, LLC sold 1.2 Cr shares for ₹181.2 Cr. Lightspeed India Partners III, LLC received ₹47.5 Cr from the sale of 31.5 Lakh shares.

Lightspeed India Partners II recorded the highest return multiple among the three vehicles at around 10.9X.

Among other selling investors, Accel clocked a 19.5X return. However, Creovate Innovation sold shares at 0.9X its acquisition cost, taking a loss on the stake sold.

Zetwerk Cofounders Pocket ₹423 Cr 

Zetwerk cofounders Amrit Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan collectively pocketed around ₹423 Cr through the OFS, selling approximately 1.4 Cr shares each for ₹211.4 Cr apiece.

Following the sale, Acharya retains 10.1 Cr shares worth ₹1,525.1 Cr at the IPO price, while Ramakkrushnan retains 11.4 Cr shares valued at ₹1,721.4 Cr.

Cofounders Rahul Sharma, Vishal Chaudhary, and Ankit Fatehpuria also sold shares through the OFS. The RHP categorised the three under “individual selling shareholders”.

Sharma and Chaudhary each pocketed around ₹26 Cr by selling approximately 17.2 Lakh shares, while Fatehpuria received ₹34.3 Cr from the sale of 22.7 Lakh shares.

The shareholder payouts formed part of Zetwerk’s ₹5,012.3 Cr IPO, comprising a fresh issue of ₹2,830 Cr and an OFS of up to 14.45 Cr shares worth ₹2,182.3 Cr at the upper end of the price band.

Founded in 2018, Zetwerk operates a manufacturing platform serving businesses across industrial and consumer goods categories.

It combines capacity from third-party suppliers and its own facilities to manage manufacturing orders across sectors including renewable energy, consumer electronics, aerospace, defence, oil and gas, and industrial automation.

Ahead of the issue, Zetwerk raised ₹2,251.2 Cr from anchor investors. Domestic mutual funds, including SBI Mutual Fund and ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, accounted for around 46% of the anchor book. Global investors, including Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, also participated.

On the financial front, Zetwerk’s operating revenue from continuing operations rose 55.4% to ₹4,117.9 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹2,649.4 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Its total net loss narrowed 46.4% to ₹733 Cr from ₹1,368.5 Cr.

Of the latest quarterly loss, ₹668.9 Cr came from discontinued operations, while continuing operations accounted for ₹64.1 Cr. The year-ago quarter included ₹803.2 Cr in exceptional charges from continuing operations and the ₹453 Cr impairment charge in the discontinued business.

item.title: Ola Electric Rights Issue: Motilal Oswal, Calliope Apply For 2.39 Cr Shares
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Calliope Capital Advisors have applied for a combined 2.39 Cr shares in Ola Electric’s ₹1,000…
item.content:encoded:
Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Calliope Capital Advisors have applied for a combined 2.39 Cr shares in Ola Electric’s ₹1,000 Cr rights issue against entitlements transferred by two promoter group entities.

The electric two-wheeler maker said in an exchange filing that Motilal Oswal Financial Services applied for 1.28 Cr shares against rights entitlements renounced by ANI Technologies. Calliope Capital Advisors applied for another 1.10 Cr shares against entitlements transferred by Indus Trust.

Calliope Capital Advisors LLP is an investment vehicle owned by Navin Agarwal, group MD of Motilal Oswal Financial Services.

Both investors submitted their applications before 11:00 IST on the opening day of the issue, covering the full entitlements transferred to them.

Renouncing a rights entitlement means transferring the right to subscribe to new shares to another investor.

ANI Technologies, which operates the Ola Cabs business, and Indus Trust held 3.47% and 2.98% stake, respectively, in Ola Electric as of June 30, according to the company’s letter of offer. Ankush Aggarwal, brother of founder Bhavish Aggarwal, serves as the trustee of Indus Trust.

Meanwhile, CMD Bhavish has committed to subscribing to his full rights entitlement. Promoter group members have also committed to subscribing to their entitlements or transferring them within the permitted categories, including to specified investors.

Earlier this month, Aggarwal pledged a 4.32% stake in Ola Electric to fund his participation in the rights issue.

Another Round Of Fundraising

The rights issue, which closes on October 30, comprises up to 37.03 Cr partly paid-up shares priced at ₹27 apiece. Investors must pay ₹16.20 per share on application and the remaining ₹10.80 through a subsequent call.

Ola Electric plans to allocate ₹350 Cr towards repaying or prepaying borrowings, including accrued interest and applicable prepayment penalties, and ₹400 Cr towards organic growth. The remaining net proceeds will fund general corporate purposes.

The fundraise follows the company’s ₹780.24 Cr qualified institutional placement (QIP) in June, with some proceeds from earlier capital raises yet to be deployed.

As of September 20, 2026, ₹139.21 Cr of IPO proceeds allocated towards debt repayment, organic growth, and general corporate purposes remained unutilised. Another ₹190.77 Cr from the QIP remained unutilised across these common objects, according to the letter of offer.

The fundraise comes at a time when Ola Electric is stepping up investments in its battery cell manufacturing and battery energy storage system businesses.

On the financial front, its consolidated net loss narrowed 22% YoY to ₹336 Cr in Q1 FY27. However, operating revenue plunged 45% YoY to ₹455 Cr. Sequentially, revenue rose 72% from ₹265 Cr, while loss narrowed from ₹500 Cr.

Shares of Ola Electric ended today’s trading session 3.21% lower at ₹31.94 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: Tonbo Imaging Cofounders Rake In ₹137 Cr From IPO
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Tonbo Imaging’s promoters and investors have realised substantial gains from the company’s IPO, which closed earlier this week post witnessing…
item.content:encoded:
Tonbo Imaging’s promoters and investors have realised substantial gains from the company’s IPO, which closed earlier this week post witnessing an overwhelming demand from investors. 

The company’s three cofounders — CEO Arvind Lakshmikumar, CBO Ankit Kumar and chief commercial officer (CCO) Cecilia D’Souza — collectively pocketed ₹137.2 Cr from the defence tech company’s ₹852 Cr IPO. 

CEO Lakshmikumar raked in ₹80.5 Cr by offloading 11.5 Lakh shares at the upper end of the ₹665-700 price band. He continues to hold around 38.18 Lakh shares, making him one of the largest shareholders of Tonbo Imaging. 

Cofounder Kumar, who serves as the CBO and CRO of Tonbo, offloaded 5.8 Lakh shares worth ₹40.6 Cr and continues to hold 24.6 Lakh shares. Meanwhile CCO D’Souza, offloaded around 2.3 Lakh shares for ₹16.1 Cr.

The largest selling shareholders in Tonbo Imaging’s IPO were its related entities, Bengaluru-based CEAQ Technologies Pvt Ltd and Singapore-based CEAQ Technologies Pte Ltd. The cofounders are the directors of these aforementioned entities as well. 

While CEAQ Technologies Pvt Ltd  offloaded its entire shareholding of around 50 Lakh shares for  ₹350 Cr, the Singapore-based entity sold 41.6 Cr shares to rake in ₹291 Cr. The Singapore-based entity continues to retain 1.05 Cr post the IPO. 

Early Investors Cash In

Among other shareholders, Artiman, an early-stage sector agnostic venture fund, has made ₹13.8 Cr by selling 2 Lakh shares, clocking a return multiple of 4.8X on its investment. It will retain another 2 Lakh shares, valued at ₹13.8 Cr at the upper price band.

Amit Dilip Shah, who is a partner at Artiman, individually sold 84,000 shares for ₹5.9 Cr at ₹700 apiece, translating to a 4.1X return, while his remaining 1.4 Lakh shares are worth ₹9.8 Cr.

Ramesh Radhakrishnan, also a partner at Artiman, offloaded 80,000 shares for ₹5.6 Cr, realising a 4.8X return on his initial investment. He will retain 1.2 Lakh shares valued at ₹8.7 Cr.

Promoter group entity Vinimaya Advisory LLP sold 3.4 Lakh shares for ₹23.8 Cr, implying a 3.6X return multiple. It will retain 3.2 Lakh shares worth ₹22.4 Cr.

Tonbo’s Road To The Bourses

The trio cofounded the defence tech company in 2003 as a defense electronics and embedded vision business. The company grew into a major global OEM for thermal imaging cores, weapon sights, and missile guidance systems serving government agencies, military organisations, and defense contractors across 24 countries.

The company’s operating revenue declined 22.7% to ₹362.6 Cr in FY26 from ₹469.1 Cr in FY25. Net profit fell to ₹50.8 Cr from ₹72.8 Cr in the previous year. In Q1 FY27, the company reported operating revenue of ₹36 Cr and a net loss of ₹17.7 Cr. The Indian government is a primary customer, making up 71% of Tonbo’s revenue in FY26. 

Tonbo Imaging’s ₹852 Cr IPO consisted entirely of an offer for sale (OFS) component of up to 1.22 Cr equity shares, with no fresh issue component. The IPO valued the company at ₹4,009.8 Cr (about $480 Mn) at the upper end of the price band.

The IPO closed for subscription on October 19 with a 136X oversubscription. Investors bidding for 115.87 Cr shares against the 85.26 Lakh shares on offer. The allotment of shares materialised today.

Ahead of the IPO, Tonbo Imaging allotted 36.5 Lakh shares to 43 anchor investors raising ₹255.4 Cr. 12 domestic mutual funds, SBI Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset, anchored the IPO.

item.title: Manufacturing Startups To Watch: 5 Startups That Caught Our Eye In October
item.dc:creator: Ankush Das
item.description: India’s manufacturing story is moving beyond assembling finished products. Startups are developing specialised components, materials and engineering systems that power…
item.content:encoded:
India’s manufacturing story is moving beyond assembling finished products. Startups are developing specialised components, materials and engineering systems that power industries ranging from electric mobility and aerospace to energy storage and computing infrastructure.

The semiconductor industry offers one indication of this shift. At SEMICON India 2026 in September, the government outlined the next phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, spanning chip design, materials, manufacturing equipment, fabrication, advanced packaging and research. The push reflects India’s ambition to build domestic capabilities across the semiconductor value chain.

Policy support is also extending to other manufacturing-intensive sectors. On October 13, the Ministry of Heavy Industries extended the bid submission deadline for a programme to establish 10 GWh of advanced chemistry cell manufacturing capacity for grid-scale energy storage. The initiative is part of the government’s effort to strengthen domestic battery manufacturing.

These developments are creating opportunities for startups building real technologies behind industrial growth. However, developing a promising technology is only the starting point. Startups must validate their products, establish reliable production processes and translate engineering capabilities into commercially viable businesses.

Against this backdrop, Inc42 is back with the October edition of its ‘Five Manufacturing Startups To Watch’. This edition features Nautical Wings Aerospace, Magron Novus, NuSynth, Refroid and Xbattery Energy, five startups working across aerospace propulsion, electric motorcycles, chemical process innovation, data centre cooling and battery management systems.

With that said, here are the five manufacturing startups that caught our eye in October.

Editor’s Note: This list is not a ranking. It is a curated selection of manufacturing startups that have stood out to the Inc42 editorial team this month.

Nautical Wings Aerospace | Developing Electric Propulsion Mechanism For Aircraft

Aircraft propulsion systems must balance power, efficiency and reliability against strict constraints on weight and operating conditions. As electric aviation and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) evolve, developing propulsion systems suited to these requirements could open up opportunities for specialised aerospace manufacturers.

Bengaluru-based Nautical Wings Aerospace is developing electric propulsion systems, motors and composite components for aircraft and UAVs. Founded in 2020, the startup also offers custom engineering capabilities for aviation applications. Its product portfolio includes fixed-wing UAV propulsion configurations with rotor sizes of up to 120 inches and power outputs of up to 150 kW.

The company’s work spans electric motors, propulsion integration and lightweight composite components, bringing several critical elements of aircraft propulsion engineering under one roof. Its focus is on developing indigenous hardware for aviation and unmanned platforms.

Nautical Wings operates in India’s emerging electric aviation market, which is projected to grow at a CAGR of 7.8% through 2029. Its progress will depend on validating its systems for specific aircraft applications and establishing repeatable manufacturing processes. 

Magron Novus | Fully Forged Carbon Fibre EVs

Building an electric motorcycle involves more than replacing a petrol engine with an electric motor. Manufacturers must engineer the powertrain, battery architecture and vehicle controls to deliver the performance riders expect. Bengaluru-based Magron Novus is attempting to bring these elements together through its own technology stack.

The startup is developing electric motorcycles and related technologies, including wireless power transfer and connected riding features. Founded in 2022, the startup showcases two platforms: the C-20, designed for everyday riding, and the H-35, aimed at the performance segment.

According to the company’s published specifications, the C-20 features a 22.5 kW motor, while the H-35 has a 35 kW motor. Its proprietary technology stack includes the Apex Drive system, battery architecture and vehicle intelligence features. The startup is also developing wireless power transfer technology and a virtual assistant to enhance the charging and riding experience.

E2Ws command a significant share of India’s booming electric vehicle market, which is poised to reach $132.2 Bn by 2030, according to Inc42’s India’s Electric Vehicle Startup Landscape Report. A healthy uptick in sales supports this market’s rally. In September, total E2W sales stood at 2.07 Lakh units, a 12.2% month-on-month increase from 1.84 Lakh units registered in August. 

Magron’s ability to turn its technology into reliable, manufacturable products and bring its motorcycles to market will determine how it develops in India’s increasingly competitive electric mobility sector.

NuSynth | Re-Engineering Chemical Manufacturing Processes

Chemical manufacturers often face challenges when developing processes for complex molecules. Existing synthesis routes can involve high material costs, difficult reaction conditions, safety risks or production steps that become harder to control at commercial scale. Improving these processes can therefore be as important as developing new chemical products.

Bengaluru-based NuSynth Technologies is a chemical manufacturing startup focused on process innovation for complex chemistry. Founded in 2026, the company aims to redesign chemical synthesis rather than rely solely on incremental improvements to existing methods. Its initial focus areas include pharmaceutical intermediates and electronic chemicals, with the ambition to develop proprietary process technologies for global markets.

The startup combines chemical research with an AI-enabled platform that uses experimental data to guide subsequent research and development. By recording experimental outcomes as structured data, the platform aims to prioritise future experiments and accelerate the development and commercial scale-up of chemical processes.

NuSynth’s operations include an R&D facility and pilot plant in Mysuru, alongside a Bengaluru facility under development. The company also reports working with more than 20 manufacturing partners across India, providing a potential route from process development to commercial production. Its services include custom synthesis, process development, scale-up and commercial supply.

NuSynth operates in India’s speciality chemicals market, valued at approximately $37 Bn in FY25, according to NITI Aayog’s report on India’s chemical industry. The segment accounts for around 18% of the domestic chemicals industry and includes high-value products used in pharmaceuticals, electronics and other industrial applications.

Refroid | Developing Cooling Systems For AI Infrastructure

Data centres require cooling systems. As facilities accommodate increasingly intensive workloads, conventional air-cooling approaches can face efficiency and capacity constraints. Liquid cooling offers another route, transferring heat more directly from computing equipment to a cooling system.

Hyderabad-based Refroid Technologies is an industrial machinery manufacturer developing cooling solutions for data centres and other mission-critical computing applications. Founded in 2021, the company focuses on liquid cooling technologies for hyperscale facilities, edge computing and high-performance computing environments.

Its technology portfolio includes immersion cooling, direct-contact liquid cooling, coolant distribution units and hybrid load banks used in testing environments. These systems are designed to support the thermal management requirements of high-performance computing. 

Refroid has also highlighted its work on indigenous cooling technologies. The company announced a collaboration with Bharat Petroleum Corporation to develop an indigenous liquid coolant and has introduced domestically developed coolant distribution units for liquid-cooled data centres.

The startup operates in India’s data centre industry, where installed capacity increased from approximately 375 MW in 2020 to around 1,500 MW by 2025, according to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.

Xbattery Energy | Building Indigenous Battery Management Systems

Batteries are central to electric vehicles and renewable energy storage, but their performance and safety depend on the electronics that monitor and control them. Much of this technology remains import-dependent, creating an opportunity for Indian manufacturers to develop indigenous battery management systems.

Hyderabad-based Xbattery Energy is a deeptech startup manufacturing battery management system (BMS) electronics for electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Founded in 2024 by Satish Reddy, Sonu Mishra and Varshith Veeramaneni, the company aims to replace imported electronics with locally developed hardware and software.

Its flagship platform, BharatBMS, supports applications ranging from 5 kWh home backup systems to megawatt-scale energy storage and high-voltage electric vehicles. The company also offers battery monitoring through a cloud platform, allowing customers to track battery parameters and diagnostics. Its customers include automotive and battery manufacturers, although names remain confidential under non-disclosure agreements.

Xbattery operates in India’s BMS market, valued at approximately $281.6 Mn in 2024 and projected to reach $699.6 Mn by 2029, growing at a compound annual growth rate of 20%, according to MarketsandMarkets’ India BMS market report. The market covers electronics used to monitor and manage rechargeable batteries across electric mobility and energy storage applications.

item.title: Binny Bansal-Backed ShopOS Launches AI Creative Platform Sloosh For Individuals
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Binny Bansal-backed AI startup ShopOS has launched Sloosh, a self-service platform that makes the image and video generation technology it…
item.content:encoded:
Binny Bansal-backed AI startup ShopOS has launched Sloosh, a self-service platform that makes the image and video generation technology it uses for enterprise clients available to individual creators and small businesses.

Speaking to Inc42, ShopOS cofounder Ajay PV said Sloosh targets creators, designers, photographers, video editors and small businesses who want to generate visual content using AI tools without engaging its enterprise creative team.

“ShopOS owns the outcome for mid and large brands. Sloosh goes after a much bigger market: anyone who makes visual content needs creatives every day,” he said.

The platform is being opened to users globally, with paid subscription plans starting at $19 per month.

Launched today, the platform operates on a subscription model, with paid plans starting at $19 per month globally.

Ajay said the decision to build a self-service product followed interest from smaller brands and individual creators who could not afford ShopOS’ enterprise retainers.

“Some of our smaller brands couldn’t afford the retainers and asked us to turn the technology into a product they could use. The idea had been brewing for a while, and over the last three months, we worked on packaging the image and video orchestration engine we had built to generate millions of creative assets for our brands into a product called Sloosh,” the cofounder added.

Sloosh brings third-party AI image and video models into a single platform, allowing users to generate content from prompts and templates. It also offers reusable workflows called Spaces and a visual canvas, Spacelab, for building or modifying these workflows.

Spaces allow users to repeat a creative task with different inputs without rebuilding prompts and settings each time. The platform also supports batch generation, enabling users to produce multiple images and videos through the same workflow.

Users can also access human creative experts for more complex projects, according to the startup.

Sloosh supports connections with AI assistants through model context protocol (MCP), allowing users to request image and video generation from compatible tools. The startup said it is also launching an Adobe After Effects plugin and plans to add more integrations.

To attract users, ShopOS plans to work with creators and build communities across markets. Users will also be able to publish and share their Spaces.

Sloosh is currently part of ShopOS, but the team is open to exploring a restructuring depending on the platform’s growth, Ajay said.

ShopOS Eyes Global Expansion

Founded in 2025 by Sai Krishna V K and Ajay, ShopOS builds AI tools and services for ecommerce brands across catalogue operations, category management, pricing, promotions, recommendations, and marketing.

The cofounders previously built augmented reality and AI commerce startup Scapic, which Flipkart acquired in 2020.

ShopOS raised $20 Mn from Binny Bansal’s investment vehicle 3STATE Ventures in June last year to develop its products, onboard brand partners, and expand its team.

Under its managed services model, ShopOS delivers finished creative assets, with its team reviewing and refining AI-generated content before handing it over to clients.

Ajay said the startup currently serves around 30-40 brands in India and a few in the US. It has also secured US contracts worth around $500,000.

Over the next year, ShopOS aims to expand its enterprise customer base to more than 100 brands in India and 40-50 brands in the US.

Its clients include Kareena Kapoor-backed Fizzy Globlet, Van Heusen, among others. The startup claims its services have reduced clients’ production budgets by nearly 90%.

item.content:encoded:
Update | October 22, 16:51

Delhi-based B2B travel tech startup TravClan has raised a $5 Mn funding round comprising a mix of equity and debt. While Walmart-owned ecommerce major Flipkart and Singapore-based investment firm August One subscribed to the equity portion of the round, Trifecta Capital provided the debt financing.

“The next generation of travel software will not just help sellers search faster. It will increasingly execute work for them. Our ambition is to make TravClan the infrastructure that any travel business can build on instead of having to recreate the entire travel stack itself. This capital allows us to invest aggressively behind that opportunity,” said TravClan CEO and cofounder Arun Bagaria.

Original | October 5, 18:51

Walmart-owned Flipkart picked up a minority stake in Delhi-based B2B travel tech startup TravClan to bolster its international travel offerings, expand holiday packages offered by subsidiaries Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel as well as enhancing on-ground support across. 

The ecommerce giant also aims to leverage the partnership to expand its own curated international leisure offerings by tapping into TravClan’s technology and partner network. 

On the other side of the table, the fresh capital infusion will support TravClan’s team expansion in business development, engineering, and destination operations, as well as allow for further investments in global supply, technology, and destination expansion. 

“Travellers today are looking for more than a flight or hotel booking. They want a holiday that is curated around their interests and supported throughout the journey. TravClan’s supplier network and destination capabilities will help us build that experience across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel,” said Nishant Verman, Flipkart’s SVP, Corporate Development and Partnerships. 

Founded by Arun Bagaria, Chirag Agrawal, and Ashish Thapliyal in 2018, TravClan assists travel agents to build and grow online businesses. It works with over 15,000 travel agents to customise and book real-time packages, hotels, and activities. 

The startup’s cap table also includes angel investors like Cars24 cofounders Vikram Chopra and Mehul Agrawal and Trip.com’s Travis Katz, as well as institutional investors like Leo Capital. 

Flipkart’s Diversification Push

For Flipkart, the travel tech investment adds on to its push to build out its other business verticals beyond its flagship ecommerce platform. 

While the company has been eyeing new entries in the food delivery and the event ticketing industry, it has been aggressively doubling down on its quick commerce arm, Flipkart Minutes.

Ahead of its annual Big Billion Days, the ecommerce giant announced that it has expanded its dark store network to nearly 1,200 Flipkart Minutes microfulfillment centres across 150-plus cities. The company is now expected to add another 1,000 dark stores by mid-2027 or the Big Billion Days sale of 2027.

In recent years, it has also expanded its in-house Flipkart Travel beyond flight booking services into bus bookings and hotel bookings. Cleartrip, an online travel aggregator which Flipkart acquired in 2021, also later expanded into corporate travel. 

Besides, Flipkart made some additional investments in AI startups last week. Its investment arm Flipkart Ventures backed Alive, an AI-powered platform for live consumer experiences, and Keploy, a native-AI software testing platform. 

To date, Flipkart has made over 20 startup investments via Flipkart Ventures across AI, consumer internet, fintech, e-commerce adjacencies and logistics tech. 

It claims to support portfolio ventures with strategic mentorship, operational expertise and access to its ecosystem in order to help them scale, besides the capital they get.

Foodtech major Swiggy reported a consolidated net loss of ₹922 Cr in the September quarter of FY27, narrowing 16% from ₹1,092 Cr in the year-ago quarter. However, its loss widened 17% from ₹791 Cr in the preceding quarter.

Operating revenue increased 36% YoY and 11% QoQ to ₹7,571 Cr. Including other income of ₹212 Cr, total income stood at ₹7,783 Cr.

Swiggy’s consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹760 Cr from ₹695 Cr a year earlier and ₹651 Cr in Q1 FY27, with higher losses at Instamart and its newer businesses weighing on profitability.

Across its consumer-facing businesses, gross order value (GOV) increased 25% YoY to ₹20,793 Cr. Average monthly transacting users rose 21% to 27.8 Mn.

Total expenses increased 30% YoY to ₹8,703 Cr.

Swiggy’s consolidated cash balance stood at ₹13,662 Cr at the end of September, down ₹705 Cr from the preceding quarter.

Instamart Steps Up Investments Ahead Of IOCC Conversion

Swiggy’s quick commerce arm Instamart reported operating revenue of ₹1,306 Cr, up 33% YoY and 6% QoQ. Its segment loss widened to ₹764 Cr from ₹739 Cr a year earlier and ₹651 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Adjusted EBITDA loss increased to ₹895 Cr from ₹849 Cr a year earlier and ₹778 Cr in the preceding quarter. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved marginally to -9.7% of GOV from -9.8% in Q1 FY27.

Swiggy said it believes Instamart’s adjusted EBITDA losses peaked in Q2 FY27. It expects another quarter of double-digit sequential net order value (NOV) growth in Q3 FY27, alongside an improvement of around 100 basis points in adjusted EBITDA margin.

Instamart’s GOV increased 31% YoY and 17% QoQ to ₹9,230 Cr during the September quarter. NOV, which excludes discounts from GOV, rose 35% YoY and 13% QoQ to ₹6,594 Cr.

However, its contribution margin deteriorated 82 basis points sequentially to -1% of GOV. Swiggy attributed the decline to targeted pricing investments to reactivate dormant users and encourage repeat purchases, changes in customer and category mix, and the initial costs of new dark stores.

The renewed spending follows Instamart’s achievement of contribution breakeven in Q1 FY27, after which Swiggy stepped up investments to accelerate growth.

Instamart added 1.3 Mn average monthly transacting users sequentially, taking the total to 14.8 Mn. Orders increased 29% YoY to 130.3 Mn, while net average order value rose 4% to ₹506.

It also added 69 dark stores during the quarter, taking its network to 1,240 stores across 133 cities.

Alongside these investments, Swiggy said Instamart’s transition to an inventory-led model will begin in mid-Q3 FY27 and take two to three quarters to complete.

The update follows the earlier shareholder approval to cap foreign ownership at 49.5% on a fully diluted basis, enabling Swiggy’s transition to an Indian-owned and controlled structure.

Swiggy said inventory ownership could improve Instamart’s contribution margin by around 80 basis points once fully implemented, while giving it greater control over assortment, pricing, and availability.

The company also expects its working capital cycle to improve by eight to 10 days, offsetting the additional investment required to hold inventory on its balance sheet.

Food Delivery Posts Records

Swiggy’s food delivery business reported operating revenue of ₹2,338 Cr, up 22% YoY. Segment profit increased 39% YoY to ₹349 Cr.

“Our food delivery business delivered its highest ever profits and margins while we continue to unlock new category growth through Toing, our standalone offering for affordable meals,” Swiggy cofounder, MD, and group CEO Sriharsha Majety said.

Food delivery GOV increased 18% YoY and 6% QoQ to ₹10,054 Cr. The business posted record adjusted EBITDA of ₹341 Cr, compared with ₹240 Cr a year earlier and ₹292 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Its adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 3.4% of GOV from 2.8% a year earlier. Swiggy attributed the improvement to advertising-led monetisation, delivery efficiencies, and operating leverage.

Bolt and its ₹99 Store together accounted for more than 25% of food delivery volumes.

The company retained its full-year food delivery GOV growth guidance of 18–20%, excluding Toing, after growth exceeded 20% YoY in September.

Meanwhile, its affordable meals app Toing, now present in more than 50 cities, continued to attract new and dormant users. Swiggy said two in three new Toing users were either first-time Swiggy users or users who had been inactive for a long time.

The company said Toing could help lift combined food delivery marketplace growth to 25-30%. In some cities, Toing’s order volumes have already reached 20-30% of core food delivery volumes.

Swiggy said repeat-user unit economics had turned positive in Toing’s earliest launch cities. However, the offering still requires improvements in monetisation and costs to make it sustainable.

It expects Toing’s investment outlay to remain within a limited range in the near term, with spending primarily directed towards customer acquisition and supported by its existing technology and execution infrastructure. Swiggy expects greater clarity on the model’s scalability over the next one to two quarters.

Toing remains part of the platform innovations segment, whose adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹162 Cr from ₹131 Cr in the preceding quarter.

Meanwhile, Swiggy’s out-of-home consumption business, which includes Dineout and Scenes, reported GOV of ₹1,508 Cr, up 35% YoY. It posted adjusted EBITDA of ₹8 Cr, marking its seventh consecutive profitable quarter on this metric.

Shares of Swiggy ended today’s trading session 5.01% lower at ₹211.30 apiece on the BSE.

item.content:encoded:
Japanese-themed dining chain Harajuku Tokyo Cafe has raised $3 Mn (around ₹28 Cr) in a pre-Series A funding round led by ZeroW, with participation from existing investors Indian Angel Network (IAN) and Samved VC.

The round also saw participation from new investors, including Blume Founders Fund, Brijesh Parekh Family Office, Epigamia cofounder Rahul Jain, among others.

The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its outlet network by opening 10 outlets in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chandigarh, over the next two quarters. 

It also plans to operationalise central kitchens in Mumbai and Bengaluru by December 2026.

Founded in 2021 by London School Of Economics (LSE) alum Gaurav Kanwar, Harajuku operates Japanese-themed dining outlets in Delhi NCR and Mumbai. It operates a casual dine-in chain, Harajuku Tokyo Cafe, and QSR-chain Harajuku Bakehouse.

Harajuku Bakehouse contributes about a third to the startup’s top line. It claims to have sold more than 1,000 loaves of bread per week on Blinkit in Delhi NCR.

Since raising its seed round of ₹19 Cr in August 2025, Harajuku claims to have doubled both its outlet count and overall revenue.

“Our focus has been to build the operational infrastructure required to support consistent quality as we expand. We have invested in centralised kitchens and systems that provide daily visibility into outlet performance, ingredients and costs. This foundation will support our next phase of growth. We aim to achieve ₹100 Cr in revenue this financial year and build on that momentum in the years ahead,” Kanwar said.

The fundraise comes amid the growing popularity of café culture in India, driven by increasing consumer interest in niche and international food offerings.

According to the Swiggy-Kearney ‘How India Eats 2025’ report, the country’s food services market is projected to grow from $78 Bn in 2025 to $120-125 Bn by 2030, with the organised segment expected to expand at roughly twice the pace of the unorganised market.

item.title: Anthropic Takes On OpenAI, Meta With New Proactive AI Agent Claude Duet
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Anthropic has unveiled Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent designed to monitor connected apps, prioritise tasks, and carry out work…
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic has unveiled Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent designed to monitor connected apps, prioritise tasks, and carry out work in the background, including when users switch off their devices.

The offering targets professionals and small business owners. Powered by Claude Opus 5.5, it is available as a research preview through a waitlist for Claude Pro and Max subscribers in the US.

Users can access Claude Duet through standalone iOS and Android apps or on Claude’s website. It is included in existing Pro and Max subscriptions but shares usage limits with other Claude products. Background checks count towards these limits, while complex assignments consume more usage, Anthropic said.

Unlike conventional AI chatbots, Claude Duet is designed to identify work that needs attention without waiting for a prompt. It sends users a daily briefing covering important items across connected apps, including emails and calendars, and provides updates when tasks are completed or require a decision.

Users can assign tasks through text or voice messages, ranging from scheduling meetings and drafting email replies to building dashboards, financial forecasts and web applications. The agent can also search past conversations and use existing Claude memories, skills and connected apps.

Claude Duet connects with more than 6,000 tools and plugins available through the Claude Marketplace, including Gmail, Slack, QuickBooks, Stripe, Gusto, LinkedIn, DocuSign, HubSpot and Shopify.

For instance, it can identify unpaid invoices through QuickBooks or Stripe and draft payment reminders. It can also prepare payroll information, draft job postings, create follow-up emails using customer and deal histories, and help businesses set up and manage online stores.

The agent runs on its own cloud-based virtual machine with a browser, allowing it to continue working even when users close the app or switch off their devices. Anthropic said it checks connected accounts every few hours rather than continuously, partly to limit subscription usage.

Claude Duet can also help users make business purchases through Link, Stripe’s digital wallet, and Shop Pay. Payments require user approval, while Link uses a virtual card to avoid sharing the user’s actual card number. Integration with 1Password for accessing saved website logins is also planned.

Anthropic said the agent requires approval before sending messages, making payments, signing documents or deleting information. Trading securities and transferring money between accounts remain prohibited, even with user approval. Users can disconnect apps, and only they can mark tasks as finished.

Safeguards And Early Limitations

Anthropic said Claude Duet includes safeguards designed to prevent unauthorised actions, prompt injection, and sensitive data leaks. Prompt injection involves malicious instructions hidden in content an agent encounters, such as emails or websites.

The protections include an automated system that assesses proposed actions and controls designed to keep passwords and sign-in tokens out of the agent’s direct view.

A separate message-checking system is designed to block requests to share highly sensitive information, including credit card numbers and government identification. Other sensitive information, such as health and personal finance details, can be shared only on explicit user instructions, Anthropic said.

The company said Claude Duet has undergone adversarial testing and external penetration testing, and is covered by its public bug bounty programme.

However, Anthropic acknowledged that the early version may misinterpret conversations, misjudge urgency, or miss information arriving between checks. It is currently better suited to work assignments than personal errands, such as booking tickets, and users cannot yet view its browser.

The launch adds to the growing competition in always-on AI agents that work across apps with limited human intervention. OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse target similar use cases, while Bengaluru-based Emergent’s Wingman handles tasks across email, calendars, and workplace software through WhatsApp and Telegram.

As agents gain access to more business systems, their permissions and accountability are also coming under scrutiny. Recently, CERT-In warned about unauthorised AI agent access to Indian organisations’ systems, highlighting the risks associated with deploying increasingly autonomous tools.

Anthropic said feedback from early users will inform further development. The research preview does not currently include Team and Enterprise subscribers.

item.title: Chapter Homes Bags ₹63 Cr To Build Home & Kitchen Tech Brands
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Omnichannel furniture and home furnishings brand Chapter Homes has raised ₹63 Cr ($6.6 Mn) in a strategic funding round through…
item.content:encoded:
Omnichannel furniture and home furnishings brand Chapter Homes has raised ₹63 Cr ($6.6 Mn) in a strategic funding round through a mix of debt and equity. The fundraise valued the startup at nearly ₹1,000 Cr (around $106 Mn).

The round saw participation from Bessemer Venture Partners, Stride Ventures, comedian Tanmay Bhat and a clutch of family offices. The brand claims to have also received further commitments from undisclosed backers for a future fundraise.

In a statement, the startup said that it plans to utilise the fresh capital to strengthen product development, expand into newer categories and invest in technology and brand building. A chunk of the capital will also be used to scale its omnichannel distribution network and set up its initial offline footprint. 

“… Consumers are increasingly looking for better-designed products, trusted quality, strong functionality and a superior overall experience – online and in store – and we see a meaningful opportunity to build for those needs. That is why we are building focused brands for each category across home and kitchen,” said Chapter Homes cofounder Nitin Chugh.

Founded in 2025 by former PharmEasy executives Chugh, Akarsh Bharadwaj, Shrey Mittal, Dhiraj Jain and Dheeraj Goyal, Chapter Homes claims to be building multiple consumer brands across categories for home and kitchen needs of Indian consumers. It has already launched a home furnishing brand under HOKIPO.

Going forward, it plans to leverage synergies across supply chain, content, technology and distribution to expand into adjacent categories such as cookware, home décor and small kitchen appliances. The startup also said that it plans to leverage AI across cataloguing and demand forecasting to product assortment and customer retention to launch faster and rein in costs.

Notably, Chapter Homes is not the first home improvement startup to emerge from the PharmEasy stable. Earlier this year, AllHome, founded by PharmEasy cofounders, raised ₹200 Cr in its Series B round led by Bessemer Venture Partners. 

The fundraise comes amid continued investor interest in the home improvement and home decor segment. In August, home decor marketplace Vaaree raised ₹65 Cr in its Series A round co-led by Hero Enterprise and Cap Alpha Ventures. Prior to this, D2C homeware startup HomeEssentials also raised ₹70 Cr in its pre-Series B round led by 360 ONE Asset.

Even the adjacent kitchen tech segment is seeing healthy adoption among masses due to LPG shortages. Many Indians are now buying induction cooktops, AI-powered smart appliances and electric rice cookers and air fryers. It is this segment that Chapter Homes plans to target going forward.

But for now, Chapter Homes is eyeing a piece of the Indian home furnishing and decor market,  which is projected to become a $45.5 Bn opportunity by 2031.

item.content:encoded:
Eternal’s Q2 Profit Surge

Eternal continued to fire on all cylinders in Q2 FY27. Besides improving margins and the profit surge, the quarter also saw Blinkit accelerate its dark store network, Zomato regain its pace and Hyperpure turn profitable. But underlying all this was Eternal’s new AI bet.

Before we move ahead, here is a quick look at Eternal’s Q2 FY27 numbers:

  • Net Profit zoomed 92% YoY to ₹125 Cr
  • Operating Revenue climbed 78% YoY to ₹24,138 Cr
  • Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled YoY to ₹666 Cr 
  • Total expenses also rose 75% YoY to ₹24,166 Cr

Blinkit Powers Growth: The quick commerce vertical remained Eternal’s strongest growth engine, supported by rapid store additions, rising order volumes and improving economics across both mature and newer markets. In total, Blinkit added 308 net new stores in Q2 FY27, taking its network to 2,751. Betting on scale, the management now expects Blinkit to cross 3,500 stores by March 2027 and reach around 5,000 stores by March 2028.

Zomato Regains Pace: The food delivery business maintained steady growth, driven by an expanding user base, stabilising demand and higher ordering frequency. Strong execution across Tier II+ markets also brought healthy top line and profits, reassuring investors that the business remains a resilient cash generator to fund broader group initiatives.

The District Question: Eternal’s going-out vertical also narrowed its losses in Q2 FY27, with the company claiming that District is on trajectory towards planned breakeven by June 2027. Meanwhile, B2B vertical Hyperpure achieved a major milestone by turning EBITDA positive in Q2, driven by two-hour deliveries and rising adoption of organised procurement offerings. 

The AI Bet: Expanding beyond foodtech, Eternal also unveiled Dark, a privacy-focused AI platform to target users that seek data confidentiality and greater control over their research. Built on fine-tuned open-weight models, the new product is scheduled for global rollout in 2026 itself. As the foodtech giant further expands its AI ambitions, here is how Eternal fared on the financial front in Q2 FY27…

From The Editor’s Desk

Jio Platforms IPO Day 1

  • The digital juggernaut’s public issue was subscribed 3.15X on the first day of bidding, with investors bidding for 62.3 Cr shares against 19.75 Cr shares on offer.
  • QIBs led the charts and subscribed their quota 9.42X. NIIs and retail investors followed suit and subscribed their portions 1.68X and 0.72X, respectively. The employee portion was also subscribed 1.36X.
  • The IPO of the Reliance Industries’ digital services arm consists solely a fresh issue of up to 27 Cr equity shares. At the upper end of its ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 price band, the ₹30,213 Cr IPO will peg the company at around around ₹10.3 Lakh Cr.

Blacksmith Bags $66 Mn

  • The AI code testing startup has raised nearly ₹663 Cr in a round led by Sequoia Capital to bolster its compute infrastructure and expand its engineering team. With this, the startup has managed to double its valuation to $1 Bn within a span of two months.
  • Founded in 2024, Blacksmith operates an AI-powered cloud platform for building and testing software code. It claims to serve more than 10,000 clients and manages 10 MW of compute footprint across data centers in the United States and Europe.
  • The fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in the enterprise AI space, which is being driven by high RoI, rapid deployment of AI tools by enterprises and regulatory support. Overall, Indian AI startups raised $438 Mn in Q3 2026, up 265% YoY.

eMudhra’s Security Key Flaw

  • Eight private keys used in the digital trust company’s infrastructure were so weak that researchers could reconstruct them from publicly available certificates. As a result, Google, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft have moved to block the impacted certificates.
  • The impacted keys were not stolen from eMudhra’s systems. They were generated using extremely small, guessable values during a key-generation ceremony in April 2025, after a flaw created a new weak set of keys alongside the intended strong ones.
  • eMudhra says its root CA private keys and Indian DSC and eSign infrastructure were not affected. However, the company’s stock hit a lower circuit, reflecting investor concern over the operational and reputational consequences for the listed company.

The Mygate-AdOnMo Merger

  • The community management startup and the adtech startup are all set to merge via a share swap deal. This comes after foodtech giant Eternal’s board approved a deal to transfer its entire shareholding in the digital advertising platform to Mygate.
  • Post the merger, which is still subject to statutory approvals, Eternal will own around 4.4% in the merged entity on a fully diluted basis. Its stake in the consolidated entity is currently valued at around ₹156 Cr. 
  • The combined entity will bring together Mygate’s community platform and AdOnMo’s network of more than 55,000 digital screens across 27 cities. Overall, Mygate claims to have closed FY26 with a top line of ₹232 Cr with an EBITDA margin of 10-12%.

Aye Finance’s Q2 Show

  • The listed NBFC’s net profit zoomed 151% YoY to ₹86.7 Cr in Q2 FY27. The surge in bottom line came on the back of certain one-time gains, a tighter leash on expenses and operating revenue growing a healthy 18% YoY to ₹514.4 Cr in the quarter. 
  • On the operational front, Aye Finance’s AUM rose 26% YoY to ₹7,597 Cr in Q2, while loan disbursements jumped 10% YoY to ₹1,403 Cr. Its active customer base expanded 18% YoY to 6.94 Lakh, with the lender adding 49,150 new borrowers during the quarter.
  • The expansion was accompanied by an improvement in asset quality. Aye Finance’s gross non-performing assets ratio declined to 4.2% from 4.5% in the preceding June quarter. Meanwhile, credit costs fell to 3.8% from 5% a year earlier.

Aiming For The Skies: Founded in 2022, Space Philic is building RUPAK, a 28-metre reusable launch vehicle designed to carry payloads of up to 250 kg to low-Earth orbit. The rocket uses a carbon-fibre booster and retractable landing legs, enabling it to return, land and fly again.

The Clean Propulsion: RUPAK will be powered by Shakti, a 32 kN bi-propellant, electric-fed rocket engine. Space Philic claims that its selective laser melting-based manufacturing reduces part count and weight, while the electric-pump design removes the need for turbopumps. The startup has already tested a Shakti engine prototype using GP-300, an ethanol-based propellant, and is now working towards scaling its launch system.

Beyond Satellites: The startup is also developing payload platforms for scientific experiments, biological research and defence missions. Its defence platform is designed for rapid-response launches, with a target of deploying defence payloads within 24 hours.

item.title: Karta AI Raises $3 Mn To Automate Inbound Calls For BFSI Players
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Agentic AI startup Karta AI has raised $3 Mn (around ₹28 Cr) in a seed funding round led by PeerCapital…
item.content:encoded:
Agentic AI startup Karta AI has raised $3 Mn (around ₹28 Cr) in a seed funding round led by PeerCapital and Cedar Hill Capital. The round also saw participation from Wyser VC, CDM Capital and Seedstars.

The startup intends to use the fresh capital to expand its go-to-market (GTM) strategy and distribution over the next two years. A portion will also help it expand its product development, particularly capabilities around emerging AI technologies such as self learning, cofounder and CEO Vijaypal Singh told Inc42.

Founded in 2024 by former Razorpay executives Vijaypal Singh and Abhishek Kushwaha, Karta AI offers an omnichannel customer communication platform spanning voice, chat, email and WhatsApp.

The startup focuses primarily on voice-based interactions, targeting complex inbound queries that require coordination across multiple enterprise systems rather than routine frequently asked questions. 

It claims to handle around 2 Mn customer conversations a month across more than 25 languages. According to Singh, it has 10-12 paying customers, including PhonePe, Pine Labs, Bajaj and Aavas.

Karta AI deploys its AI agents across customer servicing and retention workflows at financial institutions. 

The startup claims its agent resolves around 70% of borrower queries end to end without human intervention, reducing the cost per query by approximately 50%. These queries include requests for loan disbursal updates, statements of account, foreclosure statements and the release of property documents.

It focuses on inbound interactions, where customers contact businesses to resolve issues such as failed payments, blocked cards, loan-related queries and insurance claims. Unlike outbound calls, which businesses typically initiate for a specific purpose, inbound conversations can involve multiple queries and require AI agents to retrieve information and execute actions across several systems.

Singh said he and Kushwaha began working on Karta AI after leaving fintech major Razorpay, where they had worked on internal AI automation. The startup initially focused on chat-based automation before expanding into voice in August 2025.

Karta AI targets level 2 (L2) and level 3 (L3) queries, which require AI agents to interpret multiple customer intents, retrieve information from different systems and execute workflows. This differs from level 1 (L1) queries, such as basic FAQs or requests that can be resolved through a single API call.

For instance, a borrower may call a lender to check loan disbursal status and request a foreclosure statement in the same conversation. The agent must identify both intents, retrieve the relevant information and initiate the required workflows.

Singh said Karta AI has achieved 70-80% end-to-end automation in its inbound proof-of-concept (PoC) deployments and has won all such PoCs so far.

The focus on complex queries reflects their disproportionate cost. According to Singh, L1 queries account for 30-40% of customer service volumes but only around 10% of costs. L2 queries contribute another 30-40% of volumes, while L3 queries make up the remaining 10-20%. Together, he estimates, L2 and L3 queries account for around 80% of customer service costs.

The platform does not automate every interaction. Queries involving fraud or other high-risk matters, along with processes lacking clearly defined standard operating procedures (SOPs), are routed to human agents. Customers can also request a human representative.

How Karta AI’s AI Tech Works

Karta AI’s proprietary context engine is designed to help its agents manage multi-intent conversations. While conventional voice AI systems typically convert speech to text, process the query through a large language model (LLM) and generate a spoken response, Karta AI adds a layer that identifies customer intent and retrieves relevant enterprise data before generating an answer.

The engine draws on SOPs, knowledge bases, previous conversations and API data. This allows an agent to handle follow-up requests within the same call without treating each query in isolation.

Karta AI integrates with enterprise systems to execute customer-facing and back-office workflows. It uses models from OpenAI and Google’s Gemini family, alongside open-source models such as Kimi and Gemma, Singh said.

Its voice platform supports around 25 Indian languages, while its chat offering supports more than 200 languages. The voice system is designed to accommodate Hindi-English code-switching, regional accents and dialects, though performance varies across languages.

Given its focus on financial services, the startup has built compliance measures and guardrails into the platform. Singh said agents are tested by Karta AI’s team, customers and AI-based testing systems before deployment.

Karta AI primarily serves Indian businesses in banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), where high customer interaction volumes and complex back-office processes offer opportunities for automation. It plans to develop reusable, industry-specific capabilities before expanding into international markets.

item.title: CureBay Bags ₹100 Cr To Scale Rural Clinics Network, Enhance AI Screening Offerings
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Healthtech startup CureBay raised around ₹100 Cr ($10.6 Mn) in a pre-Series C funding round, comprising over ₹69 Cr in…
item.content:encoded:
Healthtech startup CureBay raised around ₹100 Cr ($10.6 Mn) in a pre-Series C funding round, comprising over ₹69 Cr in equity led by IvyCap Ventures alongside existing investors and around ₹30 Cr in debt from Trifecta Capital, Alteria Capital and VentureSoul Partners.

CureBay cofounder and CEO Priyadarshi Mohapatra told Inc42 that the round came amid strong investor interest. The startup will use the proceeds to expand geographically, strengthen its delivery network and invest in its AI and technology capabilities.

The healthtech startup, which currently operates in Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar,   plans to enter Telangana and Andhra Pradesh markets next. It aims to grow its network of rural clinics from 250 to 800 over the next two to three years.

CureBay connects patients in underserved areas with healthcare providers through a combination of rural clinics, local community health workers and a digital platform linking patients to doctors, hospitals, diagnostic laboratories and pharmacies. It also uses AI-assisted screening and care coordination to support patient care.

The startup is also investing in GPUs and training AI models to screen patients and assess health risks. Its existing AI products cover areas such as skin conditions, dental health and haemoglobin screening, with plans to expand these capabilities.

“We have a full suite of AI products for areas like skin, dental, and haemoglobin. We will keep adding more products and continue investing in width as well as depth,” Mohapatra said.

CureBay also runs Kavach, a subscription programme designed to encourage preventive care by offering consultations and support for medicines, diagnostics and certain hospitalisation-related costs. 

The startup claims to have served over 12 Lakh patients and connected more than 270 doctors and 1,000 healthcare professionals across 4,500 pincodes.

Prior to this round, CureBay had raised over $34.6 Mn from investors including Bertelsmann India Investments, British International Investment and Elevar Equity.

While the startup is yet to file its audited FY26 financial statements, Mohapatra said it closed the fiscal year with an annual recurring revenue (ARR) of nearly ₹170 Cr. It aims to double this figure by the end of FY27.

“We broke even at an operating EBITDA level in FY26. Currently, our monthly run rate is about ₹20 Cr, and we expect the number to grow almost 50% from now till March,” he told Inc42.

Mohapatra attributed the growth to customers spending more on CureBay as they increasingly view it as a trusted healthcare partner, alongside the expansion into new markets.

However, the startup remains loss-making at the company level. Mohapatra said entering new markets entails fresh expenditure, while profitability would depend on reaching a more stable operating scale.

“When we stop expanding and we reach a stable state, we will be net positive at a company level. So the important metric for us to track is operating EBITDA,” he said.
